provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has a stronger form of it. Every clause of (4.4) is stated for the constructed profiles, and the smoothness clause is stated on a larger set. E = sqrt(2X) F with F = phi/C is the body of leadingSwirl (sqrt(2X)/C * phi_0), and nominalCoefficients_zero_fields gives phi_0 = C * f on X >= 0, |eta| <= 1 with C = W.axis.normalization. V_0 = X v_0 is nominal_extended_flux (X * beta_n = radialFlux of the axial coefficient, on X >= 0, |eta| <= 1, with the hbase hypothesis of extended_flux_zero discharged by rfl). Smoothness: extendedCoefficient_contDiff gives ContDiff on all of R^2 for all four components (phi, U, beta = v_0, Pi) at every order n, and nominalCoefficients_smooth packages U, phi, Pi as SmoothCoefficients; restricting to [0,X_c] x [-1,1] gives the paper's clause for every X_c > 0, not just some. The Lean says strictly more (global smoothness including X < 0 via an extension, every X_c, every order). What the Lean does not state is the paper's general implication with smoothness assumed only on the closed rectangle: baseVelocity_smooth takes global ContDiff as its hypothesis, and no declaration names X_c or a closed-rectangle smoothness condition. I did not check that the modified scheme's analogous declarations (modifiedCoefficients_smooth, modified_extended_flux) beyond seeing that they exist with the same shape, and I did not trace that W.f, W.U, W.Pi are the paper's F, U, Pi beyond these identities.
